by_task.when: Federal exemptions under 11 U.S.C. § 522(d) are an allowable namespace for the case.
by_task.procedure: Treat 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) as an independently applicable alternative for every estate asset because it covers any property. Retain every applicable specific federal exemption as a separate alternative; fitting a specific paragraph does not displace paragraph (5).
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply paragraph (5) when federal § 522(d) exemptions are unavailable under the supplied allowable jurisdictions. Do not treat its dollar ceiling as an EC eligibility test.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions under 11 U.S.C. § 522(d) are an allowable namespace for the case.
by_task.procedure: For each asset independently, include 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5). Its ceiling for one debtor is $1,475 plus the unused portion of § 522(d)(1), limited to $13,950; if no qualifying residence uses paragraph (1), the ceiling is $15,425. Report the protected amount for the whole named asset: for one debtor, the lesser of asset value and that ceiling; for joint debtors, apply the ceiling separately to each equal interest under § 522(m), add the protected interests, and cap the result at the asset's whole value. Retain all specific federal alternatives.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit paragraph (5) merely because another exemption covers the asset, and do not allocate its ceiling across other assets in this independent-pair task. Do not leave a debtor's half-interest as the final whole-asset amount or double the ceiling unless § 522(m) actually applies to separate debtors.

by_task.when: Pennsylvania exemptions are an allowable namespace for the case and the item is property of the judgment debtor.
by_task.procedure: Include 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 as an independent alternative for the asset because it applies to property generally. Keep any applicable federal or Pennsylvania particular-property exemption as an additional alternative.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not treat § 8123 as displaced by a more specific exemption, and do not use it when Pennsylvania law is not among the supplied allowable jurisdictions.

by_task.when: Pennsylvania exemptions are an allowable namespace for the case and the item is property of the judgment debtor.
by_task.procedure: Evaluate 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 independently for each asset. For one debtor, protect the lesser of the whole asset value and $300. For jointly owned property with equal interests, protect up to $300 of each spouse's interest, add those protected interests, and report the resulting whole-asset amount, capped at the asset value and $600.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not allocate the monetary exemption across other assets in this independent-pair task, omit it because another exemption applies, or report only one spouse's half-interest as the final amount.

by_task.when: Oregon exemptions are allowable and the asset is personal property.
by_task.procedure: Include Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) as an independent alternative for the asset, while retaining every applicable category-specific Oregon and federal exemption.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply paragraph (p) to real property, and do not omit it merely because the asset also fits wearing apparel, jewelry, household goods, animals, vehicles, health aids, or another specific category.

by_task.when: Oregon exemptions are allowable and the asset is personal property.
by_task.procedure: For the independent Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) alternative, report the protected amount for the whole named asset as the lesser of its value and $400. Retain all independently applicable specific alternatives.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not allocate the $400 across other assets, apply paragraph (p) to real property, or double this asset-level amount solely because two debtors are present.

by_task.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is personal property used for personal rather than business purposes.
by_task.procedure: Include 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) as an independent alternative for the asset. Retain any separately applicable wearing-apparel, motor-vehicle, tools-of-trade, or prescribed-health-aid alternative.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit subsection (b) because a specific subsection also applies, and do not apply the personal-property exemptions to business-use property.

by_task.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is personal property used for personal rather than business purposes.
by_task.procedure: Evaluate 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently. For one debtor, protect the lesser of the whole asset value and $4,000. For jointly owned property with equal interests, apply $4,000 to each spouse's interest, add the protected interests, and report the whole-asset amount, capped at the asset value and $8,000. Retain every applicable specific subsection as a separate alternative.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not allocate subsection (b) across other assets, omit it when subsection (a), (c), or (e) also applies, apply it to business-use property, or leave one spouse's half-interest as the final amount.
